clue.text: £500 (double the amount in cash)

indicators.note: 'in cash' places the preceding amount inside whatever word stands for cash

parts.note: cash is money
twice £500 is £1,000, and K stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: A price tag of £500 with a bracketed aside about doubling the sum in hard cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like an aside but is the wordplay: K (a thousand, double 500) goes inside MONEY.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a monkey is five hundred pounds, as a pony is twenty-five and a grand a thousand.

clue.text: One doesn't like spending time away from man

indicators.note: away from tells us one letter goes missing from the word that follows

parts.note: mister is the title for a man
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes spending time away from another person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spending time' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at spending, which is money.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hoards money and hates parting with it, so is someone reluctant to pay out.

clue.text: Negative letters from company? Impossible!

parts.note: no is a negative reply
the abbreviation for company is CO, so its letters are C and O

explanation.surface: A firm sends letters full of refusals, and the recipient exclaims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' looks like correspondence; it means the two letters of the abbreviation, spelt out with the word 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is an informal reply refusing a request because it cannot be done.

clue.text: Body of letter describes quite questionable manners

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw around it, so one piece goes round another
the body is what lies within, so the outer letters of the next word are dropped

parts.note: letter without its first and last letters

indicators.note: something questionable is suspect and unsettled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder rearranged

explanation.surface: The main text of a letter describes some fairly dubious behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of quite sits inside the trimmed letter, splitting it as ET...TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette is the code of polite behaviour in society, the accepted standards of good manners.

clue.text: Man is one (except according to Donne!)

definitions.text: Man is one (except according to Donne!)

parts.note: surface reading: a statement about mankind, echoing John Donne's line that no man is one
setter's reading: the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea, a piece of land surrounded by water

explanation.surface: A quip that every man stands alone, correcting the poet Donne who said the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Donne wrote 'No man is an island'; the clue contradicts him because here Man is the Isle of Man, which plainly is one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is a self-governing piece of land surrounded by sea between Britain and Ireland.

clue.text: Heading for Sandwich in small craft

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of Sandwich
in, meaning fashionable, is hip
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Small boats making for Sandwich, a port town in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants 'small craft' together; small is a separate piece and craft alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft is a plural-friendly word for vessels, and ships are seagoing vessels.

clue.text: Looking to the sky, weighs up a task — it's taken on if really necessary

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking upward means the letters are read from bottom to top
taken on means taken aboard, so the letters are carried inside the preceding words

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of weighs, up, a and the start of task

explanation.surface: A stargazer sizes up a job they would accept only if forced.
explanation.definitionFit: At a push is a British idiom for 'if absolutely needed' or 'only with effort'.

clue.text: Passes Morlocks' prey, left for fuel

parts.note: to pass away is to die
in H. G. Wells's The Time Machine the subterranean Morlocks feed on the Eloi
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone walks past the creatures the Morlocks hunt, left behind as fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: Passes looks like moving by; it means dies.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel oil is the heavy petroleum fuel burned in diesel engines of lorries and trains.

clue.text: Mystical style of Gangnam artist?

parts.note: PSY is the South Korean singer of the 2012 hit Gangnam Style
chic is stylishness

explanation.surface: Asks whether the mystical-looking dance of a K-pop star counts as a style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gangnam Style' reads as one phrase, but style and the artist are separate pieces, with the artist's piece coming first.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychic describes powers beyond the physical, such as clairvoyance, close in sense to mystical or occult.

clue.text: After work, a priest knocks off

indicators.note: after being worked, the letters have been kneaded into a different order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman clocks off at the end of the working day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocks off' pretends to mean finishing work; here it is the definition, meaning copies illegally.
explanation.definitionFit: To pirate a film or design is to produce an unauthorised copy, which is to knock it off.

clue.text: Handy plants for sandy shade?

parts.note: surface reading: convenient garden plants
setter's reading: handy as relating to part of the hand, the trees named after it shading desert sands

explanation.surface: Recommending useful plants to give shade in a sandy garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Handy means 'of the hand', not useful; the inner face of the hand gives the trees their name, and they shade beaches and oases.
explanation.definitionFit: These tall tropical trees with fan-shaped fronds grow on beaches and desert oases, giving shade.

clue.text: Island natives spooked Argonauts and, ultimately, Jason

indicators.note: spooked creatures scatter in all directions, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the name that follows

parts.note: the last letter of Jason

explanation.surface: Jason and his Argonauts, landing on an island, are frightened by the locals.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek myth pulls toward a Mediterranean island, but the natives are apes of Borneo and Sumatra.
explanation.definitionFit: Orang-utans are great apes found in the wild only on the islands of Borneo and Sumatra.

clue.text: Employed setters and someone more senior

parts.note: the setters refer to themselves as us
ED is the editor, who outranks the setters

explanation.surface: A workforce list: the crossword setters and their boss, all on the payroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Something employed has been put to use or made use of, as a tool is.

clue.text: German publican's spirit

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for German
a publican is the host or landlord of a pub

explanation.surface: A German pub landlord's drink, a schnapps perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirit in a pub suggests liquor; here it is the supernatural kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is the spirit of a dead person said to appear to the living.

clue.text: Ordered cigs, unopened beer, or household supplies

indicators.note: ordered means arranged afresh, so the letters are put into a new sequence
unopened means the opening letter of the next word is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then losing its first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopping order of cigarettes, unopened beer, or other things for the home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like 'bought'; it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Groceries are food and everyday goods bought for the home from a shop or supermarket.

clue.text: One suspends cuts, recounting encounter with leader of 9

indicators.note: recounting means telling, so we hear the word spoken rather than see it written

parts.note: to encounter is to meet
Captain Hook leads the pirates (the answer to 9) in Peter Pan

explanation.surface: Someone who stops financial cuts recounts meeting a leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuts look like budget cuts; they are cuts of meat hung up by a butcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher hangs carcasses and joints from a sharp metal hook, so the hook holds up the cuts.

clue.text: Trump's slogan boosted men struggling against legendary warrior

indicators.note: in a down clue, boosted means pushed upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: Make America Great Again, Donald Trump's campaign slogan

indicators.note: struggling men are thrashing about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the fodder
on can mean against, as in leaning on

explanation.surface: A political slogan rallies men to fight a mythical champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the Greek king who led the army against Troy in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Spooner's 'kick in the pants' drink

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the phrase must be said with its initial sounds exchanged

parts.note: a kick in the pants is a boot to the rear

explanation.surface: A drink with a real kick, as Spooner might put it.
explanation.definitionFit: Root beer is a sweet fizzy soft drink flavoured with sassafras root, popular in North America.

clue.text: Teaching paper will be in Spanish as part of the bigger picture

parts.note: TES, formerly the Times Educational Supplement, is a British teachers' paper
será is Spanish for 'will be'

explanation.surface: An educational newspaper will appear in Spanish as part of a wider plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one small tile among many making up a mosaic image.

clue.text: From the mouth, heard by the ear

indicators.note: heard tells us to take the word as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: spoken from the mouth is oral

explanation.surface: Sound travels from the speaker's mouth and is heard by the listener's ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Aural means relating to the ear or hearing, so something aural is taken in by listening.

clue.text: Part exchange delivered: you are last to receive transport

indicators.note: exchange means swapping things round, so these letters change places

parts.note: the fodder rearranged
you are in text-message shorthand

indicators.note: last to points at the final letter of the next word

parts.note: final letter of receive

explanation.surface: A car part-exchange deal is done, and the buyer gets their new vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Part exchange is a British trade-in; here the phrase splits. Transport means ecstasy, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To be transported is to be carried away with joy, so transport is a state of ecstatic delight.

clue.text: Rocks back, kisses me, gently content

indicators.note: back tells us to read the hidden letters from right to left
content means what is held inside, so the letters sit within the following words

parts.note: the letters straddling the end of kisses, me, and the start of gently

explanation.surface: A lover rocks back and kisses gently, contentedly.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocks looks like a verb of swaying; it is the noun, slang for jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocks is informal slang for precious stones, especially diamonds, so they are gems.

clue.text: Might those they work with be stingy?

definitions.text: Might those they work with be stingy?

parts.words: Might those they work with be stingy?
parts.note: surface reading: a question about whether some workers' colleagues are mean with money
setter's reading: stingy as having stings, so the workmates are insects that sting

explanation.surface: Wondering aloud whether certain people's colleagues are tight-fisted.
explanation.walkthrough: Stingy is read as 'full of stings': the people work with bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Beekeepers tend hives of bees, insects that sting, so their working companions are literally stinging.

clue.text: Wild country with river running through shrubby area

indicators.note: something running through another passes inside it

parts.note: the bush is wild uncultivated country, especially in Australia
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A river flows through wild scrubland.
explanation.definitionFit: Brush is land covered with scrub and small bushes, a shrubby stretch of ground.

clue.text: Scored and wore away missing veneer

indicators.note: a veneer is a thin outer layer, so the front letter is stripped away

parts.note: to grate is to wear away by rubbing

explanation.surface: A surface was scratched and worn down until the veneer came off.
explanation.walkthrough: Scored looks like scratched; it means given a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rated has been assessed and given a mark, as a film is scored out of ten.

clue.text: Ernie and Ritchie meet Alec, perhaps

parts.note: Ernie Wise was the straight man of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise
Guy Ritchie is the British film director

explanation.surface: Two British entertainers bump into a third man called Alec.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the surnames' partners: each piece is the other half of a famous name.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is a know-all, and a wise guy is the same kind of cocky person.

clue.text: Behaves badly — boorish tussling's no good

definitions.note: a verb phrase; the answer is the transitive verb 'insults'

indicators.note: boorish behaviour is rough and disorderly, so the letters are knocked about
no good means without the letter for good, so that letter is struck out

parts.note: taken as written; G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone misbehaves by brawling in a boorish, unpleasant way.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who insults another is being rude and offensive, a form of bad behaviour toward them.

clue.text: Batman's thus indicated cloak?

parts.note: no letters of its own: the name is split into bat and man, and 'thus indicated' says to read those halves as instructions
the first half of Batman: to bat is to hit, or swat
the second half of Batman: a man is referred to as he

explanation.surface: Is the caped crusader's cape what he is famous for?
explanation.walkthrough: Batman splits into bat and man; the question mark warns of the trick, and the cape is a fitting nod.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap or envelop someone in fabric, much as to cloak them.

clue.text: Like 13as, having no right to short notice

indicators.note: having no right means lacking the letter for right, so it is taken away

parts.note: short of a target is under it
an ad is a notice advertising something

explanation.surface: Someone is given no right to be told anything at short notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 13as refers to the answer at 13 across, ghosts. R is the abbreviation for right.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghosts belong to the undead, beings dead yet still active among the living.
